Starts sound effect A. The effect number times three indexes the effect table at $35A4, one entry for each of the three voices ($80 and up leaves that voice alone); each voice used gets its pattern pointer from $35CE/$35E2 and a fresh state. Plays only when the sound option $A706 is 1 (effects) and the start-of-stage tune ($073A) has finished. X and Y are kept
Pattern command $92: instrument n from a second table at $35F6, seven bytes as for $287E (attack/decay, sustain/release, waveforms, gate-off point and trill)
Marks voice X finished and switches its gate off; no instruction in this listing calls it

Starts tune X (X is the tune number times six, an offset into the tune table at $2DC2). Returns at once when the sound option $A706 is 1 (effects). $2480 is the entry that skips that test, used for the title and start-of-stage tunes

Clears the player's state ($067B-$0733), silences all 25 SID registers, then for each voice reads the first entry of its order list (an $FD byte first sets the voice's transpose) and points the voice at that pattern ($2DE0/$2E03). Every voice starts on the next tick, at full volume with the filter off

The music player, called from the raster interrupt. A counter in $EA runs 0 to 5 and the player skips the sixth call, so it plays five ticks in every six frames. For each voice it steps the pattern ($25F7), then the pulse sweep ($2ACB), frequency slide ($2B32), arpeggio ($2B88) and filter sweep ($2C31) that the note turned on, and ends with the drum sounds at $2BC0

One tick of voice X. Counts down the note's length and, while it runs, handles the gate: switching the gate off a set number of ticks before the end ($06A9/$06AF), or the trill at $2770. When the length runs out it reads the next pattern byte at $2656: $80 and up is a command, dispatched through the table at $2D9C/$2DAF; $60 is a rest; anything else is a note, transposed, looked up in the frequency tables $2CA6/$2D05 and started with the instrument's waveform, followed by its length
Low byte of the command handler's address, written at $2762 from the table at $2D9C
High byte of the command handler's address, written at $2768 from the table at $2DAF; the JMP at $276D goes there
Trill: when the instrument's flag $06A6 has bit 7 set, the voice switches between its note ($06B2) and a second note ($06B5) every $069A ticks, re-gating each time
Sets voice X's frequency to note Y from the tables at $2CA6 (low) and $2D05 (high), keeping a copy in $0682/$0685 for the slide

Pattern command: end of pattern. Steps the voice's order list ($D0+voice). In the order list $FC n repeats the next pattern n times, $FD n sets the transpose, $FE lo hi jumps to another place in the list, $FF stops the voice; any other byte is the next pattern number, which is read at once
Writes voice X's kept frequency ($0682/$0685) back to the SID; no instruction in this listing calls it

Pattern command: instrument n. Copies seven bytes from the instrument table at $2ECE (attack/decay, sustain/release, gate-on waveform, gate-off point, trill flag and speed, gate-off waveform) into the voice's state and writes the envelope to the SID
Pattern command $86: sets how many ticks before a note's end its gate goes off ($06A9/$06AC) and the waveform it switches to ($0694)
Pattern command: sets the second note of a trill ($06B5/$06B8)
Pattern command: pulse-width sweep n. Six bytes from the table at $2F45: how many ticks to sweep up and down, the step each way and the starting width
Pattern command: frequency slide. The two bytes after it point to a slide list that $2B32 reads
Pattern command: arpeggio. The two bytes after it point to a list: its speed and length, then the note offsets that $2B88 cycles through

Pattern command: drum n. Five bytes from the table at $2E26 give the waveform and frequency lists $2BC0 plays, their length and the envelope; the next byte is a pitch offset and the one after the note length

Pattern command: filter n. Routes this voice through the filter ($2A41 holds each voice's routing bit), sets the volume and filter mode from the next byte, and loads the cutoff sweep from the table at $2F8D for $2C31
Operand of the STA at $29FF, read by the instruction stream only
Each voice's bit in the filter's routing register $D417 (1, 2, 4), with the resonance in the top four bits
Pattern command $8B: takes this voice out of the filter's routing ($0720 = 0, $D417 = 0)
Pattern command: ends the trill by clearing the second note ($06B8 = 0)
Pattern command $8D: notes keep their gate on to the end ($06A9 = 0)
Pattern command: notes take their length from the pattern again ($072E = 0)
Pattern command: every following note is n ticks long, so the pattern can leave the lengths out ($072E/$0731)
Pattern command: writes a value to a SID register: the next byte is the value, the one after the register number

Voice X's frequency slide. The list holds entries of three bytes (ticks, then a 16-bit step added to the frequency each tick); an entry starting $4C is a jump to the address after it
Voice X's arpeggio: every $06FA ticks plays the next offset from its list, added to the note, wrapping after $06FD entries

Where the loader jumps after loading this level. Sets $0782 to 2, then $8005 sets up the machine and runs the title screen

Interrupts off, I/O and RAM banked in ($01 = $35), stack reset, both CIAs' interrupts off. Builds the title display ($A912, $E8E2, $E087, $E8C5, $E89D), starts tune 1 and the raster interrupts ($8510), and waits at $8045 for fire, checking the keyboard for the level-skip word each frame ($F69E). Fire stops the music, clears the score, starts tune 3 and the clock and power, and falls into stage one at $80B1
Stage one, the street: stage number $E000 = 0, sets up the stage ($81A6), the player ($E1B1) and the enemy list (attack script at $A1C3), then runs the walking stage's main loop at $8121
Stage two, the hostage: stage number 1, the crosshair stage. Sets up the gunman and hostage ($951D) and runs its own main loop at $8176
Stage three, the second street: stage number 2, attack script at $A1D8, then the walking stage's main loop at $8121

Main loop of the walking stages (one and three), once a frame: player, enemies, shots, scroll, pickups, collisions, clock ($ABFC), power and the end of stage ($AD20). On the frames when the music counter $EA is 0, one in six, it also runs the slower jobs: the stage tune's end, damage ($ACD1), score display and keyboard
Main loop of the hostage stage, once a frame: crosshair, the gunman's movement ($82B4) and animation ($832A), the shot ($81F7), power, end of stage, clock and the hostage timer ($81BD)
Sets up a stage: colours, display, scroll position, player state and power display, then builds the stage's screen at $98FB

Hostage stage: when the clock reaches 0:00 before the gunman is shot, the hostage dies. Costs 14 units of power, plays effect 9, shows the gunman's frames for that (set 3) and starts a 150-frame wait ($07C3); when that runs out the game moves on to stage three

Hostage stage, when a shot was fired ($07C6): works out the crosshair's column and row against the gunman's position. Rows between the limits at $825C and $8271 for that column hit the gunman: a hit counts in $07C7, freezes him for 12 frames, plays effect 0 and scores. Rows down to $8286 hit the hostage instead: 4 units of damage and effect 10

Enemy X's death: the first frame plays effect 11 and turns it yellow. Every six frames it shows the next frame from the list at $846A in its three sprites. At the end the enemy either goes, or, when it carried a pickup ($73,x), becomes the pickup: its sprite from $845C, colour from $8464, lying for 200 frames

Removes any enemy that has left the play area (Y below $2C or from $E2, X 0 or from $AA); a slot with Y 0 is empty and left alone
Counts down three frame timers, $0780, $078F and $07A6, stopping each at zero

Returns Z clear only on a new press of fire on joystick port 2; holding the button returns Z set

Title screen: when a key is pressed ($8B03), switches the sound option $A706 between 0 (music) and 1 (effects); $84F7 then writes the option's 14-letter name from $E7B3 (16 bytes a name) into the title screen at $437D, in light blue
Points the IRQ vector at the title screen's interrupt ($8539) and the NMI vector at $85E7, which only acknowledges CIA2 and returns, so RESTORE does nothing. Raster interrupt on line $20
Title screen raster interrupt, once a frame on line $20: plays the music unless $ECCC is set, and counts the frame in $E703

In-game interrupt on raster line 0: clears extended colour mode, sets the vertical scroll to 3, and starts CIA2's timer B as a one-shot of $199C cycles, whose NMI ($85A2) comes about 101 lines later. Then lays out the sprites ($8721), counts the frame, lets the next interrupts in and runs $9A86 and the music

NMI from CIA2's timer, part way down the screen, where the status panel ends and the play area begins. Turns on extended colour mode together with multicolour, a mode the VIC-II draws as black, so the switch is hidden; sets the play area's scroll ($07CF, $07D0), its memory ($0679 into $D018) and VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF), then sets a second NMI ($85EF) $169 cycles later
A zero byte between two interrupt routines
NMI handler that acknowledges CIA2 and returns: RESTORE is ignored
Second NMI, about eleven lines later: ends the black band by turning extended colour mode off, so the multicolour play area shows

Called from the line-0 interrupt.
